text: Define cloud and on-prem infrastructure in human-readable configuration files that can be versioned, reused, and shared
quote: HashiCorp Terraform is an infrastructure as code tool that lets you define both cloud and on-prem resources in human-readable configuration files that you can version, reuse, and share.

text: Define resources that span multiple cloud providers and services
quote: You define resources, which may be across multiple cloud providers and services.

text: Create an execution plan to preview the changes Terraform will make to infrastructure
quote: The `terraform plan` command creates an execution plan, which lets you preview the changes that Terraform plans to make to your infrastructure.

text: Apply automatically generates a plan, prompts for approval, then performs the operations
quote: Terraform automatically creates a new execution plan as if you had run terraform plan, prompts you to approve that plan, and performs the indicated operations.

text: Execute the operations proposed in a plan with terraform apply
quote: The `terraform apply` command executes the operations proposed in a Terraform plan.

text: Skip interactive approval with -auto-approve so apply runs without confirmation
quote: You can pass the `-auto-approve` option to instruct Terraform to apply the plan without asking for confirmation.

text: Save a generated plan to a file with -out and later apply that saved plan file
quote: You can use the optional `-out=FILE` option to save the generated plan to a file on disk, which you can later execute by passing the file to `terraform apply`

text: Show a JSON representation of a plan file, including configuration and current state
quote: For Terraform plan files, `terraform show -json` shows a JSON representation of the plan, configuration, and current state.

text: The -json flag streams machine-readable JSON UI messages, one per line, for plan, apply, refresh, and test
quote: For long-running commands such as `plan`, `apply`, `refresh`, and `test`, the `-json` flag outputs a stream of JSON UI messages.

text: Inspect a plan or the current state in human-readable form with terraform show
quote: Use the command to inspect a plan to ensure that the planned operations are expected, or to inspect the current state as Terraform sees it.

text: Use speculative plans to check the effect of changes before code review
quote: developers can use speculative plans to verify the effect of their changes before submitting them for code review.

text: Import existing infrastructure resources into state from the CLI so Terraform can manage them
quote: You can import an existing resource to state from the Terraform CLI.

text: Generate the matching configuration for imported resources using the import block
quote: If you want to generate the accompanying configuration for imported resources, use the `import` block instead

text: Modify state from the CLI using the terraform state command
quote: Terraform provides the terraform state command to perform basic modifications of the state using the CLI.

text: State command output is structured to work with Unix tools such as grep and awk
quote: The CLI usage and output of the state commands is structured to be friendly for Unix tools such as grep, awk, etc.

text: State maps real-world resources to configuration, tracks metadata, and improves performance for large infrastructures
quote: Terraform uses your workspace's state to map real world resources to your configuration, keep track of metadata, and to improve performance for large infrastructures.

text: Store state in HCP Terraform or a remote backend for secure storage and team collaboration
quote: We recommend storing state in HCP Terraform or a remote backend to securely store state and collaborate with team members.

text: Write tests that check module changes don't break anything, running against short-lived test resources
quote: Terraform tests let authors validate that module configuration updates do not introduce breaking changes. Tests run against test-specific, short-lived resources, preventing any risk to your existing infrastructure or state.

text: Mock data returned by providers during terraform test runs
quote: Terraform v1.7.0 introduced the ability to mock data returned by the providers during a `terraform test` execution.

text: Define policies that validate Terraform plans against security rules and best practices
quote: Policies are rules for Terraform runs that let you validate that Terraform plans comply with security rules and best practices.

text: Write custom policies using Terraform policy, Sentinel, or OPA
quote: Write custom policies using Terraform policy, Sentinel, or OPA

text: View and override policy enforcement results in the workspace UI
quote: View and override policy enforcement results in the workspace UI.

text: Official MCP server gives AI models real-time access to registry provider docs, modules, and policies
quote: The Terraform Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enhances AI models with real-time access to current Terraform provider documentation, modules, and policies from the Terraform registry.

text: MCP integration makes AI-generated Terraform configuration more accurate and actionable
quote: AI enhancement: Enables more accurate and actionable Terraform configuration generation.

text: Create, update, and delete workspaces with variables, tags, and run management
quote: Workspace operations: Create, update, delete workspaces with support for variables, tags, and run management.

text: Publish and consume providers, modules, and policies on the public Terraform Registry
quote: Anyone can publish and consume providers, modules, and policies on the public Terraform Registry

text: Create reusable configurations with modules
quote: Create reusable configurations with modules.

text: Search and filter providers and modules by tier in the Registry
quote: Select a provider or module card to learn more, filter results to a specific tier, or use the search field at the top of the Registry.

text: Automatically download providers published on the Terraform Registry
quote: Terraform can automatically download providers that are published on the Terraform Registry.

text: Build your own provider so Terraform can interact with a service
quote: Create a provider to allow Terraform to interact with a service.

text: Build a resource graph and create or modify non-dependent resources in parallel
quote: Terraform builds a graph of all your resources, and parallelizes the creation and modification of any non-dependent resources.

text: Perform proposed operations in the correct order, respecting resource dependencies
quote: On approval, Terraform performs the proposed operations in the correct order, respecting any resource dependencies.

text: Create a plan to destroy all remote objects with the -destroy option
quote: These include `-destroy`, which creates a plan to destroy all remote objects, and `-refresh-only`, which creates a plan to update Terraform state and root module output values.

text: Create a refresh-only plan that updates state and root module outputs to match real infrastructure
quote: These include `-destroy`, which creates a plan to destroy all remote objects, and `-refresh-only`, which creates a plan to update Terraform state and root module output values.

text: Force replacement of specific resource instances with the -replace option
quote: specifying which resource instances Terraform should replace (`-replace`), setting Terraform input variables (`-var` and `-var-file`)

text: Set input variables at plan time with -var and -var-file
quote: specifying which resource instances Terraform should replace (`-replace`), setting Terraform input variables (`-var` and `-var-file`)

text: Hosted sandbox with preinstalled tools and services for experimenting with Terraform
quote: The Terraform sandbox contains preinstalled tools and services for you to experiment with Terraform.
